content.text: Schema and seed both load cleanly. Next are the two procedures. I'm leaving out `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`, since `CALL` on a procedure that commits fails inside an outer transaction. The caller owns the transaction, and the exception block provides the rollback that `sp_monthly_report` needs.

input.content:
-- ============================================================================
-- PostgreSQL translation of the Oracle procedures in oracle/*.sql
--
-- Notes on the translation:
--   * NVL(x, y)            -> COALESCE(x, y)
--   * SYSDATE              -> now()
--   * Oracle dummy table   -> plain SELECT (no FROM clause needed in PostgreSQL)
--   * %ROWTYPE / %TYPE     -> explicit column types
--   * ROWNUM = 1 probe     -> dropped; it read a value that was never used
--   * COMMIT / ROLLBACK    -> removed. A PostgreSQL procedure that commits cannot
--                             run inside a caller's transaction, so the caller
--                             controls commit. sp_monthly_report's rollback-on-
--                             no-data is provided by the EXCEPTION block, which
--                             rolls back its own work automatically.
--   * User-defined exception e_no_data -> RAISE with a dedicated SQLSTATE
--     (no_data_found, P0002), handled by name.
-- ============================================================================

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- sp_customer_tier: aggregate active customers' orders and assign a tier.
--   GOLD >= 1000, SILVER >= 500, otherwise BRONZE.
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_customer_tier()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_tier varchar(20);
    rec    record;
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM customer_tiers;

    FOR rec IN
        SELECT o.customer_id,
               c.customer_name,
               SUM(o.order_total) AS total_spend,
               COUNT(*)           AS order_count
        FROM   orders o
        JOIN   customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
        WHERE  COALESCE(c.status, 'ACTIVE') = 'ACTIVE'
        GROUP  BY o.customer_id, c.customer_name
    LOOP
        IF rec.total_spend >= 1000 THEN
            v_tier := 'GOLD';
        ELSIF rec.total_spend >= 500 THEN
            v_tier := 'SILVER';
        ELSE
            v_tier := 'BRONZE';
        END IF;

        INSERT INTO customer_tiers
            (customer_id, customer_name, total_spend, order_count, tier, computed_at)
        VALUES
            (rec.customer_id, rec.customer_name, rec.total_spend, rec.order_count,
             v_tier, now());
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- sp_monthly_report: revenue and units sold per product category for a month.
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_monthly_report(p_month varchar)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_has_data integer := 0;
    rec        record;
BEGIN
    -- Oracle read a constant row from its dummy table here; a plain SELECT does the same.
    SELECT 1 INTO v_has_data;

    DELETE FROM monthly_report WHERE report_month = p_month;

    FOR rec IN
        SELECT p.category                                     AS category,
               COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0)  AS revenue,
               COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0)                  AS units_sold
        FROM   order_items oi
        JOIN   products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
        GROUP  BY p.category
    LOOP
        INSERT INTO monthly_report
            (report_month, category, revenue, units_sold)
        VALUES
            (p_month, rec.category, rec.revenue, rec.units_sold);
    END LOOP;

    IF v_has_data = 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'no data to report for %', p_month
            USING ERRCODE = 'no_data_found';
    END IF;
EXCEPTION
    WHEN no_data_found THEN
        -- Mirrors Oracle's e_no_data handler: the block's work is rolled back.
        NULL;
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE;
END;
$$;

-- ============================================================================
-- PostgreSQL translation of the Oracle procedures in oracle/*.sql
--
-- Notes on the translation:
--   * NVL(x, y)            -> COALESCE(x, y)
--   * SYSDATE              -> now()
--   * Oracle dummy table   -> plain SELECT (no FROM clause needed in PostgreSQL)
--   * %ROWTYPE / %TYPE     -> explicit column types
--   * ROWNUM = 1 probe     -> dropped; it read a value that was never used
--   * COMMIT / ROLLBACK    -> removed. A PostgreSQL procedure that commits cannot
--                             run inside a caller's transaction, so the caller
--                             controls commit. sp_monthly_report's rollback-on-
--                             no-data is provided by the EXCEPTION block, which
--                             rolls back its own work automatically.
--   * User-defined exception e_no_data -> RAISE with a dedicated SQLSTATE
--     (no_data_found, P0002), handled by name.
-- ============================================================================

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- sp_customer_tier: aggregate active customers' orders and assign a tier.
--   GOLD >= 1000, SILVER >= 500, otherwise BRONZE.
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_customer_tier()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_tier varchar(20);
    rec    record;
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM customer_tiers;

    FOR rec IN
        SELECT o.customer_id,
               c.customer_name,
               SUM(o.order_total) AS total_spend,
               COUNT(*)           AS order_count
        FROM   orders o
        JOIN   customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
        WHERE  COALESCE(c.status, 'ACTIVE') = 'ACTIVE'
        GROUP  BY o.customer_id, c.customer_name
    LOOP
        IF rec.total_spend >= 1000 THEN
            v_tier := 'GOLD';
        ELSIF rec.total_spend >= 500 THEN
            v_tier := 'SILVER';
        ELSE
            v_tier := 'BRONZE';
        END IF;

        INSERT INTO customer_tiers
            (customer_id, customer_name, total_spend, order_count, tier, computed_at)
        VALUES
            (rec.customer_id, rec.customer_name, rec.total_spend, rec.order_count,
             v_tier, now());
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- sp_monthly_report: revenue and units sold per product category for a month.
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_monthly_report(p_month varchar)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_has_data integer := 0;
    rec        record;
BEGIN
    -- Oracle read a constant row from its dummy table here; a plain SELECT does the same.
    SELECT 1 INTO v_has_data;

    DELETE FROM monthly_report WHERE report_month = p_month;

    FOR rec IN
        SELECT p.category                                     AS category,
               COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0)  AS revenue,
               COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0)                  AS units_sold
        FROM   order_items oi
        JOIN   products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
        GROUP  BY p.category
    LOOP
        INSERT INTO monthly_report
            (report_month, category, revenue, units_sold)
        VALUES
            (p_month, rec.category, rec.revenue, rec.units_sold);
    END LOOP;

    IF v_has_data = 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'no data to report for %', p_month
            USING ERRCODE = 'no_data_found';
    END IF;
EXCEPTION
    WHEN no_data_found THEN
        -- Mirrors Oracle's e_no_data handler: the block's work is rolled back.
        NULL;
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        RAISE;
END;
$$;
